# Small Language Models Technical Whitepaper

## Section 1: Memory and Parameter Profiles
Small Language Models (SLMs) typically operate in the sub-4-billion parameter domain, enabling on-device execution on consumer hardware with 6GB to 8GB of VRAM.

### Model A: Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct
Qwen 2.5 3B is commercially classified as a 3B model, although its exact published parameter count is approximately 3.09 billion parameters. It utilizes a 32,768-token native context window and standard GQA (Grouped Query Attention). It requires approximately 1.9 GB of VRAM when quantized to 4-bit (Q4_K_M).

### Model B: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
Meta released Llama 3.2 3B Instruct with an official count of 3.21 billion parameters. It supports a context window of up to 131,072 tokens and features specialized multilingual capabilities across 8 core languages.

### Model C: Qwen3 1.7B
Qwen3 1.7B represents an ultra-compact architecture containing 1.70 billion parameters. It loads within 1.4 GB of system memory, providing high tokens-per-second throughput (often exceeding 70-90 tokens per second on laptop GPUs).

## Section 2: Retrieval and Vector Storage
In local RAG architectures, documents are chunked using semantic sentence boundaries and transformed into dense vectors via sentence-transformers models such as `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, which outputs 384-dimensional normalized vectors stored in persistent ChromaDB collections.

## Section 3: Safety Guardrails and Database Interaction
When connecting SLMs to relational databases, direct raw SQL generation poses catastrophic hallucination and injection hazards. The laboratory mandates a two-phase confirmation protocol: the model produces a validated structured operation proposal, trusted Python backend code applies parameterized SQL statements, and destructive UPDATE or DELETE mutations require manual user confirmation before commit.
